task.description: WF-02 Step 3 scope test for REQ-142 (replace 118 inline hex color literals with CSS custom property references across 15 files under web/src/components/canvas/).
acceptance_criteria: scope test correctly applied against actual Step 2b artifacts_out

result.summary: Out of scope — no executable surface requiring new tests. Scope test reasoning: Step 2b produced .tsx/.ts files under web/src/components/canvas/ — file extension heuristic says YES, but the real test per WF-02 Step 3 is whether a test would exercise real behavior or just assert an implementation detail. The change is a pure inline-style token substitution: 118 occurrences of hex color literals (e.g. #FF0000) replaced with CSS custom property references (e.g. var(--color-error)) in style={} props across 15 canvas component files. No conditional logic, no props, no event handlers, no state, and no data flows were changed — only the literal string value of inline color properties. A test asserting style.color === 'var(--color-error)' would verify the refactoring artifact itself, not component behavior, and would add no protection against any behavioral regression. This falls squarely into the 'satisfy a gate without substance' anti-pattern (core-directives.md). AC-3 independently confirms this: it requires the existing 184-test suite pass unchanged with no assertions altered to accommodate the color-value change, meaning those tests already adequately exercise the canvas components at their behavioral surface. All four acceptance criteria are verifiable by command-output demonstration (grep for remaining hex literals, git diff scope check, npm test output, npm run guards output) — RELEASE-VALIDATOR verifies them directly from the Step 2b artifacts and gate output, not from new test results. Steps 3b and 4 skipped.
result.next_action: Route directly to RELEASE-VALIDATOR (Step 5) — Steps 3b/4 skipped.
